events.instrument: Decreto de Necesidad y Urgencia N° 366/2025 (B.O. 29/5/2025), art. 3
events.what_changed: Before: health care and social assistance could not be denied or restricted 'in any case' to any foreigner, whatever their migration status. After: only emergency care is guaranteed to all. Permanent residents get equal access to the public health system. Everyone else gets routine care in national-run facilities only on showing health insurance or paying in advance. This narrows the protection from all migrants to permanent residents (plus emergencies for all).
events.passage: ARTICULO 8° — En casos de emergencia, no podrá negársele ni restringírsele el acceso a la asistencia social o a la atención sanitaria a todos los extranjeros que lo requieran, cualquiera sea su situación migratoria. Los extranjeros residentes permanentes podrán acceder al sistema de salud público en igualdad de condiciones que los ciudadanos argentinos. Por fuera de los supuestos establecidos en los párrafos precedentes, en los establecimientos que brinden atención sanitaria administrados por el ESTADO NACIONAL, solo se brindará tratamiento médico o atención sanitaria habitual contra la presentación de un seguro de salud o la previa cancelación del servicio

events.instrument: Decreto de Necesidad y Urgencia N° 366/2025 (B.O. 29/5/2025), art. 1
events.what_changed: The equal-access clause, which expressly covers health, now applies 'according to the rights and obligations of each migration category' and no longer mentions migrants' families. Equal treatment in health thus depends on residence category.
events.passage: ARTICULO 6° — El Estado en todas sus jurisdicciones asegurará el acceso igualitario de los inmigrantes a las mismas condiciones de protección, amparo y derechos de los que gozan los nacionales, de acuerdo con los derechos y obligaciones correspondientes a cada categoría migratoria, en particular en lo referido a servicios sociales, bienes públicos, salud, educación, justicia, trabajo, empleo y seguridad social. (Artículo sustituido por art. 1º del Decreto Nº 366/2025 B.O. 29/5/2025. Vigencia: a partir del día de su publicación en el BOLETÍN OFICIAL.)

events.instrument: Provincial charging schemes (Salta Feb 2024; Jujuy, Mendoza Aug 2024, Santa Cruz in 2024; Ciudad de Buenos Aires Mar 2025), as reported by Chequeado
events.what_changed: Provinces began charging foreigners without residence for non-emergency care in public hospitals. Before the DNU this ran against the then-unconditional art. 8. Foreigners' consultations fell sharply (Salta down up to 95% in some hospitals compared with 2023; Jujuy outpatient visits down 75%). This is practice evidence, not a change in national law.
events.passage: Antes de la reforma nacional, varias jurisdicciones habían implementado sus propios sistemas de cobro. Salta, Mendoza, Santa Cruz y Jujuy comenzaron durante 2024 y la Ciudad de Buenos Aires se sumó en marzo de 2025. En todas ellas se contemplaron excepciones para las emergencias.

answers.implementation_then_now: 2023: the unconditional art. 8 governed, and no charging scheme was documented. Chequeado's figures use 2023 as the baseline before Salta began charging in February 2024, which suggests foreigners were being treated without charge then. The starting rating of Usually is kept. Before 1 January 2026, Salta, Jujuy, Mendoza, Santa Cruz and Buenos Aires City began charging foreigners without residence for routine care, and their consultations fell sharply. In national hospitals, charging was not yet regulated on 1 January 2026: Resolución 1066/2026 only came in August 2026. Measured against the narrower 2026 protection (emergency care for all, equal access for permanent residents), no pattern of denial to permanent residents or of refusal of emergency care was found, so the rating is Usually. Under the old, broader standard, practice clearly worsened.

answers.notes: Citation for 1 Jan 2026: National law in Argentina protects this right only for some migrants in the Migration Law (Ley de Migraciones N° 25.871), arts. 6 and 8, as substituted by Decreto de Necesidad y Urgencia N° 366/2025. Art. 8 now guarantees emergency care to all foreigners 'whatever their migration status'. It gives equal access to the public health system only to 'permanent resident foreigners'. Everyone else (temporary, transitory and precarious residents, and irregular migrants) gets routine care in national-run facilities only 'on presentation of health insurance or prior payment'. Art. 6 now makes equal access to health depend on 'the rights and obligations of each migration category'. ICESCR art. 12 has constitutional rank under art. 75 inc. 22, but it gives no specific statutory equal-access rule. DNU 366/2025 took effect on publication (29 May 2025). It had not been rejected by both chambers under Ley 26.122 as of 1 Jan 2026: none of the sources found reported a rejection, but this was not checked directly. The Ministry of Health's procedure for national hospitals (Resolución 1066/2026, Aug 2026) falls outside the window.

provisions.instrument: Ley N° 24.464 Sistema Federal de la Vivienda

events.instrument: Decreto de Necesidad y Urgencia N° 366/2025 (B.O. 29/5/2025), art. 1
events.what_changed: Before: equal access 'for immigrants and their families' to the same protection and rights as nationals, including social services and public goods. After: the same clause applies 'according to the rights and obligations of each migration category', and families are no longer mentioned. The basis for equal access to public goods, including housing programmes, is narrowed further by residence category. The answer option does not move.
events.passage: ARTICULO 6° — El Estado en todas sus jurisdicciones asegurará el acceso igualitario de los inmigrantes a las mismas condiciones de protección, amparo y derechos de los que gozan los nacionales, de acuerdo con los derechos y obligaciones correspondientes a cada categoría migratoria, en particular en lo referido a servicios sociales, bienes públicos, salud, educación, justicia, trabajo, empleo y seguridad social.

answers.implementation_then_now: In both periods, national housing programmes such as Procrear II's Desarrollos Urbanísticos restricted eligibility to 'argentinos/as o extranjeros/as con residencia permanente'. Some local programmes are reported to require citizenship. Irregular and temporary migrants were therefore excluded in practice. No migrant-specific practice evidence showing a shift between 2023 and 2026 was found. National housing programmes shrank from 2024 for everyone, but that is not migrant-specific. The starting rating of Rarely is kept for both dates. The evidence is mostly programme rules, not documented outcomes, so confidence is low.

answers.starting_answer_concern: The starting answer rests on the original art. 6, which granted equal access to 'immigrants and their families' with no reference to status. Its downgrade to the 50-point option is justified by local and programme-level exclusions (citizenship or permanent residence), which are practice or sub-national rules rather than national law. On a strictly statutory reading, the 2023 answer could arguably have been 'Yes (including irregular migrants)'. Ley 24.464 itself was not read in this session, because the text page failed to load.
answers.notes: The answer option is the same at both dates. The change scale records 'not the same' because a cited provision (art. 6) was substantively narrowed by DNU 366/2025 with effect from 29 May 2025: equal access is now tied to each migration category. If reviewers treat a narrowing that leaves the option unchanged as 'no change', use 'There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed'. Citation for 2026: National law in Argentina protects this right only for certain migrants, in Constitution art. 14 bis (access to decent housing) and Ley 25.871 art. 6 as substituted by DNU 366/2025, which promises equal access to 'social services, public goods' 'according to the rights and obligations of each migration category'. Ley 24.464 does not set nationality criteria, but national programmes require permanent residence.
